title: Lumen Health POC — tail latency & cost breakdown
content:
Executive summary:

This doc captures the benchmarking and cost analysis we ran for the Lumen Health conversational triage POC. Goal was to characterize tail latency (p95/p99), steady-state throughput, and $/1M-token cost across model variants, hardware (A100 vs H100), and runtime knobs (batch size, KV caching, quantization). Tests used a mixed-production traffic profile to be representative of their expected load.

High-level findings (short):
- Best latency for interactive chat: H100 + fp16 + batch=1 + KV-cache warm. Typical p95: 210–360ms depending on model size.
- Cost leader: 4-bit quantized variant on A100 delivered ~3.6x cost reduction vs fp16 baseline with moderate latency increase (~+20–45% p95).
- KV cache has outsized benefit for conversational flows: warm-cache p95 improvements of 35–60% on long-session traces. Cold-cache p99 remains a risk under bursty fanout.
- For Lumen’s 80/20 short/long prompt mix, recommended default: enable KV cache, route high-QOS calls to H100 fp16 until rollout, then switch to quantized variants for bulk throughput during non-critical windows.

Objectives:
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency for candidate models across representative sequence lengths (64, 256, 1024).
- Measure tokens/sec and end-to-end throughput under steady load and under bursty fanout.
- Estimate $/1M tokens using internal cost model (instance runtime + amortized infra + infra egress).
- Validate KV-cache warm vs cold behavior and propose routing/runbook for graceful degradation.

Test matrix:
- Models tested: redwood/atlas-13b-chat (fp16), redwood/atlas-13b-4bit (4-bit quant), meta-llama-2-13b-chat (fp16), opt-6.7b-chat (fp16).
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (single GPU) and NVIDIA H100 80GB (single GPU).
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 (client-side batching via redwood-loadgen).
- Sequence lengths considered: short=64 tokens, medium=256 tokens, long=1024 tokens (generation only, prompt lengths varied).
- Traffic mix: 80% short conversational queries (<=64 tokens total), 20% long context/resume-generation (>=512).
- KV cache states: cold (first request after model spinup), warm (cache populated for conversation), partial (cache for some sessions).

Load generation and measurement details:
- Tooling: redwood-loadgen v0.9 deployed from a separate runner; collectors: Prometheus metrics + request traces to Console traces.
- Each run: 10-minute ramp, 20-minute steady window, 5-minute burst test (2x peak QPS), 10-minute cooldown.
- Measurements reported are taken from the 20-minute steady window unless noted (burst test results called out separately).

Key results (steady-state, mixed traffic):
Note: numbers below are steady-window medians and tail percentiles averaged across three runs.

1) Atlas-13b-chat (fp16) on H100:
- batch=1, seq=64: p50=42ms, p95=210ms, p99=420ms, throughput=850 tok/s, cost ≈ $42 / 1M tokens.
- batch=4, seq=64: p50=52ms, p95=270ms, p99=520ms, throughput=1500 tok/s, cost ≈ $25 / 1M tokens.
- seq=1024 (generation heavy): p95=680ms, p99=1.6s, throughput=320 tok/s.

2) Atlas-13b-4bit (A100 quantized build):
- batch=1, seq=64: p50=78ms, p95=320ms, p99=760ms, throughput=620 tok/s, cost ≈ $12 / 1M tokens.
- batch=4, seq=64: p50=96ms, p95=410ms, p99=980ms, throughput=1100 tok/s, cost ≈ $7.5 / 1M tokens.
- seq=1024: p95=1.1s, p99=2.6s, throughput=240 tok/s.

3) meta-llama-2-13b-chat (fp16) on A100:
- batch=1, seq=64: p50=60ms, p95=310ms, p99=650ms, throughput=700 tok/s, cost ≈ $50 / 1M tokens.

4) opt-6.7b-chat (fp16) on A100:
- batch=1, seq=64: p50=34ms, p95=160ms, p99=360ms, throughput=980 tok/s, cost ≈ $28 / 1M tokens.

KV-cache effects (atlas-13b-chat on H100):
- Cold-cache p95 (batch=1, seq=64): 210ms (cold-first) -> warm-cache p95: 130ms. That is ~38% improvement in p95 and p99 improves ~45%.
- For long sessions (>=512 context), cache hit ratio observed: 62% after 3-turn session.
- When bursting many new conversations concurrently (fanout), cold-cache p99 spikes to 1.8–2.4s on A100; H100 absorbs fanout better but still shows p99 spikes ~1.1–1.9s.

Burst (2x) behavior:
- With batch=1 and no autoscaling, 2x burst caused queue growth and p99 went from 420ms -> 2.1s on Atlas-13bfp16/A100.
- Enabling request routing to a cheaper quantized fallback reduced p99 spike by ~35% at the cost of lowered per-token quality (qual tests below).

Quality checks (sanity, small eval):
- We ran 200 human-readability probes comparing fp16 vs 4-bit quant for triage prompts. 4-bit produced acceptable answers in ~86% of cases; 10% had minor hallucinations or degraded fluency, 4% were unacceptable.
- For Lumen, clinical-safety-sensitive steps should route to fp16 model or require aggregator/verification logic.

Cost model assumptions:
- Instance cost (amortized infra + infra ops + GPU): A100 per GPU effective hourly = $2.75 in our internal cost model; H100 per GPU effective hourly = $4.10.
- Tokenization/IO overhead modeled at 6% of tokens/sec.
- These produce the $/1M token values above; small fluctuations possible depending on utilization and reserved capacity discounts.

Takeaways and recommendations for Lumen Health POC:
1) Default production profile (recommended):
   - Use Atlas-13b-chat fp16 on H100 with KV cache enabled for interactive, high-QoS traffic (critical triage flows).
   - Set batch target = 1–4 for latency-sensitive routes; autoscale capacity with warm pools to avoid cold-cache spikes.
   - Fall back to Atlas-13b-4bit on A100 for bulk background generation and low-criticality tasks during peak windows.
2) Routing and runbook:
   - Policy: route by intent + latency SLO. If intent == triage-critical => route to fp16/H100. Else => route to quantized/A100.
   - Autoscale policy: maintain 20% headroom for peak+burst; pre-warm GPUs when predicted activity crosses 60% of baseline.
   - KV cache policy: enable conversation-level cache with TTL=8 hours for triage sessions; provide a cached-hit fallback path.
3) Cost/quality tradeoff:
   - Expect ~3–3.6x $ savings moving from fp16/H100 to 4-bit/A100 for throughput-heavy use-cases, with a quality hit observed in ~14% of probes. Use human-in-loop for critical thresholds.
4) Risk controls:
   - Monitor p99 across routes; implement auto-failover to smaller models (opt-6.7b) or degrade gracefully to stateless summary when p99 exceeds 1.2s for >30s.
   - Add continuous eval checks (sampled prompts) for quantized outputs; trigger rollback on quality regression >8% unacceptable rate.

Action items / next steps:
- Solutions-eng: wire the routing policy prototype into the demo environment (LIN-2891) — owner: Aisha (ETA 2026-02-26).
- Prod infra: configure H100 warm-pool with pre-warm trigger at 60% predicted utilization — owner: Marisol (ETA 2026-03-05).
- Seeding: create 5k conversational prompts from Lumen anonymized dataset to feed cache warmers — owner: Liam (ETA 2026-02-22).
- Evaluate 2 additional 4-bit compiler variants for quality: quant-v2 and quant-v3; run 2k-probe evals — owner: Dmitri (ETA 2026-03-01).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need to confirm Lumen’s tolerance for 4-bit failure modes in triage-critical flows; legal & clinical signoff required.
- Confirm discount/reserved pricing for A100/H100 to refine $/token to within ±12%.
- Consider measuring multi-GPU sharded setup for Atlas-70B variant if Lumen requests larger context and higher QA.

Appendix — raw numbers (one run snapshot):
- Atlas-13b-chat/H100/batch1/short: p50=41ms, p90=168ms, p95=210ms, p99=427ms, tok/s=860.
- Atlas-13b-4bit/A100/batch4/short: p50=94ms, p90=360ms, p95=410ms, p99=980ms, tok/s=1102.
- opt-6.7b/A100/batch1/short: p50=33ms, p95=162ms, p99=378ms, tok/s=980.

If you want, I can:

- run an extended 24-hour steady-state run to refine cost numbers.

Notes: this document is a working artifact — results may change as quant variants and kernel improvements land.
